model.title: Detection model
model.description1: To automatically detect sensitive information in your documents, Rature relies on a <bold>Named Entity Recognition (NER)</bold> model. Unlike large language models (LLMs) that power tools like <italic>ChatGPT</italic>, these models are much lighter. This allows them to run entirely in your browser, without sending your data to a server.
model.description2: Currently, the model detects 4 entity types: <bold>persons</bold>, <bold>organizations</bold>, <bold>locations</bold>, and a <bold>miscellaneous</bold> category for entities identified but not classified with certainty.
model.description3: Soon, you will be able to choose from several models to refine detection according to your needs.

supported.title: Supported documents
supported.description1: Rature currently supports PDF files containing selectable text. Scans and photos of documents are not yet supported.
supported.description2: We are working to expand compatibility to other formats (Word, Excel,…). Missing a format? Feel free to send us your suggestions:
supported.feedback: Your feedback directly shapes our roadmap.

stats.title: Product statistics
stats.description1: We will be implementing usage statistics for the Rature product.
stats.description2: These statistics will be completely anonymous and will only concern the use of Rature's features, in accordance with our <link>privacy policy</link>.
stats.description3: You will be able to fully opt out of these statistics from this page.

files.title: Cached files
files.description1: Rature stores the tools needed to process your documents in your browser to avoid downloading them on every use.
files.description2: On your first use, loading may therefore take a little longer. However, these files take up space on your device.
files.description3: You can delete them at any time if you no longer wish to use Rature.

siteData.title: Site data
siteData.description: You can also delete all Rature data, including cached files and site settings. This action will reload the page and reset Rature to its original state.

observation.title: The problem
observation.description: Using AI tools often involves sharing documents containing sensitive information: names, addresses, emails, or client data.

manual.title: The manual solution
manual.description: One solution is to anonymize documents <underline>by hand</underline>: find each piece of sensitive information, hide them one by one, check and recheck.

solution.title: solves this problem
solution.p1: The tool <bold>automatically</bold> detects and masks sensitive data in your documents so you can share or analyze them safely.
solution.p2: Unlike many online services, <app/> runs entirely in your browser: your files are never sent to a server and never leave your device.
solution.p3: The project follows a simple philosophy: you should be able to use AI tools without compromising the privacy of your data.

howItWorks.title: How does it work?

step1.title: 1. Import your PDF
step1.description: Simply drag your document into the application. Processing starts immediately in your browser.

step2.title: 2. Automatic detection of sensitive data
step2.description: analyzes the document and identifies potentially sensitive information: names, addresses, emails, phone numbers, identifiers, etc.

step3.title: 3. Edit detected elements
step3.description: Detected data is highlighted in the document. You can quickly verify and adjust what needs to be anonymized (double-click to hide/add).

step4.title: 4. Review the redactions
step4.description: With one click, you can preview the anonymized document.

step5.title: 5. Export your anonymized PDF
step5.description: Download your anonymized document and use it safely: sharing, AI analysis, archiving, etc.

howItWorks.localNote: The entire process takes place <bold>100% locally in your browser</bold>.
howItWorks.noLeave: Your files never leave your computer.

openSource.title: Open source and transparent
openSource.sourceDesc: The source code is public. It can be consulted and verified. This transparency is essential for a tool that processes potentially sensitive documents.
openSource.sourceDesc2: You can review how files are analyzed, how entities are detected in the text, and how anonymization is applied.
openSource.nonDevContrib: <fiderLink>Suggest improvements</fiderLink> and we will review the feasibility!
openSource.philosophy: We believe that privacy tools must be <bold>open and verifiable to be trustworthy</bold>.

s1.title: 1. Overview
s1.p1: Rature is a tool for anonymizing PDF documents by masking sensitive information before sharing.
s1.p2: Privacy protection is a fundamental principle of the project. The tool was designed to operate <bold>without collecting personal data and without transferring documents to a server</bold>.

s2.title: 2. Document processing
s2.p1: All documents are processed <bold>locally in your browser</bold>.
s2.li1: PDF files are <bold>never sent to a server</bold>.
s2.li3: No document content <bold>is analyzed or retained by a server</bold>.
s2.p3: Processing is performed directly on your device.

s3.title: 3. Data collected
s3.p2: No element contained in the documents you use with the tool is transmitted, recorded, or analyzed by a server. The service may only measure <bold>anonymous technical information related to the application's operation</bold>, such as:
s3.li1: <bold>Page views</bold> (e.g.: the pages consulted by visitors).
s3.li4: <bold>Traffic source</bold> (e.g.: from where you've reached Rature).
s3.p3: <bold>This information cannot in any way identify a user or a document.</bold>

s4.title: 4. Cookies and trackers
s4.p1: Rature <bold>uses no cookies</bold> and installs no trackers on your device.

s5_1.title: 5.1 Transparency commitment
s5_1.p1: Even though Rature collects no personally identifiable data, we are committed to respecting the principles of the <bold>General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)</bold> and informing you of your rights. The following sections detail these rights, as well as the technical and organizational measures put in place to protect your data.

s5_2.title: 5.2 Your rights
s5_2.p1: In accordance with the GDPR and other applicable laws, you have the following rights regarding your personal data:
s5_2.li1: <bold>Right of access</bold>: You can ask us whether data relating to you is being processed and obtain a copy of such data.
s5_2.li2: <bold>Right to rectification</bold>: You can request the correction of inaccurate or incomplete data.
s5_2.li3: <bold>Right to erasure</bold> ("right to be forgotten"): You can request the deletion of your data in certain cases (e.g.: unlawfully processed data).
s5_2.li4: <bold>Right to restriction of processing</bold>: You can request the suspension of processing of your data in specific cases.
s5_2.li5: <bold>Right to data portability</bold>: You can receive your data in a structured format and transfer it to another service.
s5_2.li6: <bold>Right to object</bold>: You can object to the processing of your data for legitimate reasons.

s5_3.title: 5.3 How to exercise your rights?
s5_3.p1: Although Rature collects <bold>no personally identifiable data</bold>, you can contact us via:
s5_3.p2: We are committed to responding to your request within <bold>one month</bold> (which may be extended by two months in complex cases).

s5_4.p1: If you believe your rights are not being respected, you can lodge a complaint with the <bold>CNIL</bold> (Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés):

s7.title: 7. Hosting
s7.p1: Rature is a <bold>100% client-side</bold> service: document processing takes place <bold>exclusively in your browser</bold>, without sending or storing data on a server. However, to make the tool accessible online, the website is hosted by a <bold>third-party technical provider</bold>.

s7_1.title: 7.1 Hosting provider
s7_1.p1: The site is currently hosted by:
s7_1.p2: This provider acts as a <bold>data processor</bold> within the meaning of the GDPR (article 28) and only has access to <bold>the minimum technical data</bold> necessary for the operation of the service.

s7_2.title: 7.2 Change of provider
s7_2.p1: In the event of a change of hosting provider:
s7_2.li1: We will inform you via an update to this <bold>privacy policy</bold>.
s7_2.li2: Previously collected technical data will be <bold>deleted</bold> from the former provider before migration.

s8.title: 8. Security
s8.p1: Rature's architecture was designed to limit risks related to sensitive documents:
s8.rec2: Avoid <bold>unverified extensions</bold> that could access your data.
s8.rec3: Verify the <bold>anonymization result</bold> before sharing the document.

s9.title: 9. Disclaimer
s9.p1: Rature provides an anonymization tool <bold>without absolute guarantee</bold>. The user remains responsible for:
s9.li1: <bold>Verifying the result</bold> (e.g.: absence of residual data in the anonymized PDF).
s9.li2: <bold>Complying with applicable laws</bold> governing their documents (e.g.: copyright, professional secrecy).
s9.li3: Using the tool in a <bold>secure environment</bold> (e.g.: up-to-date browser, uncompromised network).

s11.title: 11. Changes and notification
s11.p1: This privacy policy may be updated to reflect:
s11.li3: Feedback from users or data protection authorities.
s11.howTitle: How will you be informed of changes?
s11.how1: The <bold>current version</bold> is always available on this page, with the date of the last update.
s11.how2: In the event of a <bold>substantial change</bold> (e.g.: change of hosting provider, addition of data collection), we will inform you via:
s11.how2a: A <bold>banner on the site</bold> on your next visit.
s11.how2b: An <bold>email</bold> if you have provided a contact address (e.g.: to contribute to the project).
